question:
A 7-year-old male with severe persistent asthma presents to the emergency department with
respiratory distress lasting 3 days. His history includes recent hiking in Colorado with acetazolamide
use for altitude sickness (discontinued 7 days ago), followed by a 4-day episode of vomiting and
diarrhea that resolved 2 days prior. Current symptoms include coughing, wheezing, and dyspnea.
Covid-19 vaccination is current and SARS-CoV-2 testing is negative. Physical examination reveals an
uncomfortable-appearing patient with heart rate 148/min, respiratory rate 35/min, and oxygen
saturation 91% on room air. Chest examination shows diffuse bilateral wheezing. After treatment with
multiple albuterol nebulizers, IV methylprednisolone, and magnesium, he is placed on continuous
albuterol and transferred to intensive care. The next morning, wheezing has resolved but significant
tachypnea persists. Laboratory results at 24 hours show: | | Patient value | Reference range | | --- | --- |
--- | | Sodium (mEq/liter) | 138 | 135–147 | | Potassium (mEq/liter) | 3.2 | 3.4–4.7 | | Chloride (mEq/liter) |
104 | 97–107 | | Bicarbonate (mEq/liter) | 15 | 22–26 | | Blood urea nitrogen (mg/dL) | 16 | 5–18 | |
Creatinine (mg/dL) | 0.7 | 0.3–0.7 | | Glucose (mg/dL) | 121 | 60–100 | | Venous pH | 7.25 | 7.31–7.41 |
What is the most likely cause of this patient's metabolic derangement? Answer Choices: (A) Primary
respiratory alkalosis (B) Renal tubular acidosis (C) Diarrhea (D) Dehydration-induced metabolic
acidosis (E) Lactic acidosis (F) Ingestion of acetazolamide (G) Metabolic compensation for respiratory
alkalosis (H) Magnesium-induced metabolic acidosis (I) Steroid-induced metabolic acidosis (J)
Beta-agonist induced ketoacidosis
 A. Renal tubular acidosis
B. Lactic acidosis

C. Metabolic compensation for respiratory alkalosis
D. Ingestion of acetazolamide
E. Magnesium-induced metabolic acidosis
F. Primary respiratory alkalosis
G. Steroid-induced metabolic acidosis
H. Beta-agonist induced ketoacidosis
I. Diarrhea
J. Dehydration-induced metabolic acidosis
